answer: Seeded identity windows. Each agent must register an identity behind a fresh atlas of random delay drawn from a verifiable beacon after commit. The oasis of scheduling slots is revealed only post-commit, so attackers cannot precompute which zephyr of time their duplicate lands in. Enforcement: one identity per revealed window, checked against the beacon-derived partition. Attacker cost: every duplicate needs a new hardware-timed commit and forfeits all prior scheduling position, multiplying per-identity registration work and forcing sequential re-entry.
